subject: Business Models
title: Everything-as-a-Service
description: A short lesson to help you apply Everything-as-a-Service.

hook.text: Lighting, heating, tires, and even airplane engines are now sold as subscriptions, not products.

buildup.text: Philips sells 'Light as a Service': businesses pay for illumination, and Philips owns and maintains the bulbs.

discovery.text: The seller keeps ownership, incentivizing durability. Why build stuff that breaks when you maintain it forever?

twist.text: This model aligns with sustainability. Manufacturers design for longevity when they bear replacement costs.

climax.text: Everything-as-a-Service could fundamentally reshape capitalism from ownership to access.

punchline.text: Own nothing, subscribe to everything. The product economy is ending.

quiz.question: Why does 'as a service' incentivize product durability?

details.summary: Everything-as-a-service extends the subscription model beyond software to physical goods, transportation, housing, and even clothing. Companies offer access to products through monthly payments instead of ownership, from cars and furniture to dog toys and personal styling.
details.whyItMatters: The as-a-service trend represents a fundamental economic shift from ownership to access. It changes consumer behavior, product design, and business models across every category as recurring revenue replaces one-time sales.
takeaways: Subscriptions now cover physical products far beyond digital services
Access replaces ownership across transportation, housing, and consumer goods
The model works best when products benefit from regular refreshing

faq.question: What types of physical products are successfully offered as subscriptions?
faq.answer: Cars through services like Volvo's Care subscription, furniture through Fernish, clothing through Rent the Runway, and even tires through Michelin's fleet services. Products that benefit from variety, regular updates, or maintenance tend to work best in subscription formats.

faq.question: Why do consumers prefer access over ownership for certain products?
faq.answer: Lower upfront costs remove purchase barriers. Regular refreshing satisfies the desire for novelty. Maintenance and disposal are handled by the provider. Flexibility to upgrade or cancel avoids long-term commitment..
